open_points.subject: A17 configuration schema
open_points.text: Registry's code receives each item as a field of the settings the one module that reads the environment loads; no other part of Registry reads a variable. The items are exactly these: the store's location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel
open_points.question: What are the exact environment-variable names, settings-field names and field types for every listed item, and how does each variable map to its field?
options: Use fixed derived names such as REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION and fields such as store_location
Use different fixed names such as REGISTRY_STORE_PATH
Declare the mapping in a separate settings schema
open_points.default_guess: Use REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION, REGISTRY_BACKUP_LOCATION, REGISTRY_BACKUP_KEY, REGISTRY_OWNER_CREDENTIAL and one REGISTRY_<SERVICE>_TOKEN variable, mapped to correspondingly named settings fields.

witness.initial: All required values are valid and the store location is supplied as REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION.
events: The settings module attempts to load the store-location item.
outcomes: An implementation that derives REGISTRY_STORE_LOCATION recognizes the item and starts.
An implementation that calls the same item REGISTRY_STORE_PATH treats it as missing and stops the start.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a running Registry or a missing-item diagnostic.

open_points.subject: A17 service-token presence check
open_points.text: the service tokens all four or none — none makes an owner-only start, and some but not all fail on the first missing one in rule 1's order
open_points.question: Does an environment variable that exists with an empty value count as a token being set for the all-or-none check, or as an unset token?
options: Presence of the variable counts as set, even when its value is empty
An empty value counts as unset
An empty value is a distinct malformed-present state
open_points.default_guess: Count the variable as present, apply all-or-none by presence, and only afterward reject its empty value during well-formedness or length checking.

witness.initial: Every non-token item is valid; REGISTRY_PRESUPRO_TOKEN is present with an empty value and the other three token variables are absent.
events: Registry performs the all-or-none service-token check.
outcomes: If empty means present, some but not all tokens are set and the start fails on the first missing token.
If empty means unset, none of the four tokens is set and Registry starts owner-only.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a failed start or a serving owner-only instance.

open_points.subject: A17 secret representation
open_points.text: A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at least 32 bytes long; a shorter one fails the start.
open_points.question: How is an environment-variable text value converted to the byte sequence whose length and equality are checked?
options: Require an ASCII value and count its bytes
Decode a specified encoding such as Base64 and count the decoded bytes
Count Unicode code points despite the rule saying bytes
open_points.default_guess: Treat the environment text's UTF-8 encoding as the secret bytes, count those bytes, and compare those byte sequences without Unicode normalization.

witness.initial: All configuration is valid and distinct except that one service token consists of 20 non-ASCII characters whose UTF-8 encoding exceeds 32 bytes.
events: Registry converts and validates the token.
outcomes: An implementation counting UTF-8 bytes accepts the token's length.
An implementation counting characters or requiring ASCII rejects it as short or malformed.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether Registry starts or reports the token failure.

open_points.subject: A17 failed-item diagnostic
open_points.text: a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that names the failed item and never its value
open_points.question: What exact identifier must a diagnostic use to name an item: its environment-variable name, its settings-field name, or a human-readable label?
options: Name the environment variable, such as REGISTRY_BACKUP_KEY
Name the settings field, such as backup_key
Use a human-readable label, such as backup key
open_points.default_guess: Use the canonical environment-variable name because it directly tells the owner which configuration entry is missing or invalid.

witness.initial: The backup-key item is absent and every earlier check passes.
events: Registry reaches the presence check for the backup key.
outcomes: One implementation reports REGISTRY_BACKUP_KEY as missing.
Another reports only “backup key” or “backup_key” as missing.
witness.observer: The owner and any test asserting the diagnostic see different text.
